diagnostics.message: :resource.helm_release.karpenter: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.update_kubeconfig: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references

helm_release.karpenter has an explicit depends_on on module.karpenter, but this is already established implicitly via attribute references (module.karpenter.service_account and module.karpenter.queue_name in the values template), as captured in implicit_deps.

null_resource.update_kubeconfig has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but it already depends on module.eks implicitly via the module.eks.cluster_name reference in its local-exec command (captured in implicit_deps).

null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but it already depends on module.eks implicitly via the module.eks.cluster_primary_security_group_id and module.eks.cluster_security_group_id references in its triggers block (captured in implicit_deps).

null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class has an explicit depends_on on module.karpenter, but it already depends on module.karpenter implicitly via the module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn reference in its triggers block (captured in implicit_deps).

null_resource.apply_node_pool has an explicit depends_on on helm_release.karpenter, but the same ordering is already guaranteed transitively through apply_node_pool -> null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class -> helm_release.karpenter.

null_resource.apply_node_pool has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but the same ordering is already guaranteed transitively via null_resource.update_kubeconfig -> module.eks (and null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class -> module.eks), both of which apply_node_pool already depends on.

null_resource.delete_daemonset has an explicit depends_on on module.eks, but the same ordering is already guaranteed transitively via its dependency on null_resource.update_kubeconfig, which itself depends on module.eks.

helm_release.karpenter has an explicit depends_on on data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster, but this is already established via the helm provider configuration, which references data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster; every resource of the helm provider implicitly waits for that provider configuration.

null_resource.delete_daemonset runs 'kubectl delete daemonset -n kube-system aws-node' as part of the Calico CNI migration, but it has no dependency on null_resource.create_calico_installation. Nothing in the graph orders the aws-node daemonset deletion after the Calico Installation resource is created; in a single apply these two null_resources can run concurrently, and removing aws-node before Calico is installed can break pod networking. It should depend on null_resource.create_calico_installation (bare depends_on; no data-reference fix is possible for these null_resources).
